/-- Sheaf cohomology for `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaves, the analogue of `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.
Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H` is parameterised over `Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat` only, which loses
the `k`-linear structure needed to define a genus. The result here carries `Module k` automatically
via `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.instModule`, so `Module.finrank k` is well-defined on it. It is an
`abbrev` rather than a `def` so that instance synthesis sees through the wrapper to find the
`Module k` and `AddCommGroup` instances. -/
noncomputable abbrev HModule
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) : Type (u+1) :=
  Abelian.Ext ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n

/-- The `k`-linear identification of `HModule k F 0` with the group of morphisms from the constant
sheaf at `ModuleCat.of k k` to `F`. It is `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀`
(`Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)` in any `Linear R`-enriched abelian category) specialised to the
`Linear k` enrichment of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`, which is inferred from
`HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`. On a connected proper `k`-curve this identifies
`H⁰(C, toModuleKSheaf C)` with `Γ(C, O_C)` viewed as a `k`-module. -/
noncomputable def HModule_zero_linearEquiv
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
    HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k]
      ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F) :=
  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀

/-- The `ModuleCat k`-valued cohomology of an object `X : C` with values in a sheaf
`F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`, mirroring Mathlib's
`Sheaf.H' F n X = (F.cohomologyPresheaf n).obj (op X)` for `AddCommGrpCat`-valued sheaves with
`AddCommGrpCat.free` replaced by `ModuleCat.free k`.

The codomain is `Type u` rather than `ModuleCat.{u} k`: `Abelian.Ext` returns a bare type, which
carries `Module k` through the `Linear k` enrichment via `Abelian.Ext.instModule`. As for
`HModule`, the `abbrev` form is needed so that instance synthesis finds
`Module k (HModule' k F n X)` and `AddCommGroup (HModule' k F n X)`; under `def`,
`Module.finrank` would fail to typecheck.

This is the coefficient carrier for a `ModuleCat k`-valued Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence on a
`MayerVietorisSquare`, and for the comparison
`cechCohomology_OC C 𝒰 n ≅ HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) n` on an acyclic cover; neither is proved
here. -/
noncomputable abbrev HModule' (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) (X : C) : Type u :=
  Abelian.Ext ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
    ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X)) F n

/-- The degree-zero identification for `HModule'`, the analogue of `HModule_zero_linearEquiv`: the
`k`-linear identification of `HModule' k F 0 X` with the group of morphisms from the sheafified
representable `(presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X)` to `F`. It is
`CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀` (`Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)` in any `Linear R`-enriched
abelian category) at `R = k`, using the `Linear k` enrichment of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`
obtained from `HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` via `Sheaf.linear`. It is the algebraic input for
`H⁰(C, O_C) ≃ k` on a connected proper `k`-curve. -/
noncomputable def HModule'_zero_linearEquiv
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C) :
    HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
      ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F) :=
  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀

/-- If the Hom group `((constantSheaf J _).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)` is finite over `k`, then so
is `HModule k F 0`. The equivalence `HModule_zero_linearEquiv` identifies the two `k`-modules, and
`Module.Finite.equiv` transports finiteness along it; the `.symm` puts the hypothesis on the Hom
group and the conclusion on the cohomology. For proper geometrically integral `k`-curves the
hypothesis is supplied by finiteness of the global sections. -/
theorem module_finite_HModule_zero

/-- The underlying types-valued presheaf of `Scheme.moduleKPresheaf` is that of the
structure sheaf. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKPresheafCompForgetIso :
    X.moduleKPresheaf k ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k) ≅
      X.presheaf ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat :=
  NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦ Iso.refl _) (fun _ ↦ rfl)

lemma Scheme.isSheaf_moduleKPresheaf :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (X.moduleKPresheaf k) := by
  have h : TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf (C := ModuleCat.{u} k) (X := (X : TopCat))
      (X.moduleKPresheaf k) := by
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp' (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k))
      (X.moduleKPresheaf k)]
    change Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) _
    rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_of_iso_iff (X.moduleKPresheafCompForgetIso k)]
    exact (TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp'
      (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat) X.presheaf).mp X.toSheafedSpace.IsSheaf
  exact h

/-- The structure sheaf of a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the
small Zariski site of `X`. Its sections over `U` are *definitionally*
`ModuleCat.of k Γ(X, U)` (with the `Scheme.overModule` action) and its restriction maps
are definitionally those of the structure sheaf; see `Scheme.moduleKSheaf_obj` and
`Scheme.moduleKSheaf_map_apply`. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKSheaf :
    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
  ⟨X.moduleKPresheaf k, X.isSheaf_moduleKPresheaf k⟩

@[simp]
lemma Scheme.moduleKSheaf_obj (U : X.Opens) :
    (X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.obj (op U) = ModuleCat.of k Γ(X, U) := rfl

lemma Scheme.moduleKSheaf_map_apply {U V : X.Opensᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V)
    (s : Γ(X, U.unop)) :
    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map i).hom s = (X.presheaf.map i).hom s := rfl

/-- `H⁰` of the structure sheaf of `X` over `Spec k` is the module of global sections
`Γ(X, ⊤)`, `k`-linearly (with the `Scheme.overModule` structure on the right). -/
noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKSheafHZero :
    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 0 ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, ⊤) :=
  Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat))
    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
    (X.moduleKSheaf k)

9	/-!
10	# Extension uniformity, reduced to a chart count uniform in the extension
11	
12	`ResidueField.UniformlyBoundedVanishing` writes down cluster P's gap (2) — a **single**
13	vanishing threshold `b`, chosen before the field extension `κ/k` — and proves it at no
14	curve.  The two inputs its docstring records as genuinely missing are flat base change for
15	the section spaces and a `WeilDivisor` pullback along `C_κ ⟶ C`.
16	
17	This file does **not** supply either.  What it does is remove the *cohomological* half of the
18	obstruction, using the ungated Čech formula of `ChiUnconditional.lean`:
19	
20	`h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts` says `Ȟ¹(D) = 0` iff the three chart dimensions satisfy a
21	numerical identity.  That criterion mentions **no** connecting homomorphism, no exactness
22	datum, and nothing about `κ` beyond the chart dimensions themselves.  So extension
23	uniformity follows from a chart count that is uniform in `κ` — and the residual gap becomes a
24	statement about **dimensions of section spaces under base change**, which is exactly the flat
25	base change already identified as missing, and nothing more.
26	
27	That is the honest gain: the gap does not shrink logically, but it stops being three
28	different things (vanishing + exactness + base change) and becomes one (base change).
29	
30	## The three gaps, kept apart as the task requires
31	
32	* **Single-field vanishing** — `ChiUnconditional.h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts` is an ungated
33	  *criterion*; whether its right-hand side holds at a given curve is not proved here or
34	  anywhere in AJC.  Still open, now purely a counting question.
35	* **Extension uniformity** — `uniformlyBoundedVanishing_of_uniformChartCount` below reduces
36	  it to `UniformChartCount`, a κ-uniform chart identity.  `UniformChartCount` is **not
37	  proved at any curve**; it is a hypothesis, and it is strictly stronger than the
38	  single-field count. Still open.
39	* **Global generation** — untouched here; see `GlobalGeneration.lean`.  It is proved from
40	  the ledger inputs and is *not* implied by anything in this file.

48	open scoped WithZero AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

55	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
56	
57	/-- **The κ-uniform chart count.**  A single threshold `b`, chosen before the extension `κ`,
58	above which the Čech inclusion–exclusion count computes `ℓ` on the base-changed curve.
59	
60	This is the base-change-side hypothesis, isolated.  Compare
61	`ChiUnconditional.h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts`, whose right-hand side is this identity at one
62	fixed field: `UniformChartCount` is that identity with `b` pulled outside the `∀ κ`, which is
63	precisely the uniformity the predicate `UniformlyBoundedVanishing` demands.
64	
65	It is stated with the finiteness of the three base-changed chart section spaces as explicit
66	hypotheses in the body rather than as instance binders, because on the base-changed curve
67	those instances are exactly what a base-change theorem would produce, and demanding them as
68	binders here would quietly assume the missing input. -/
69	def UniformChartCount (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
70	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
71	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) : Prop :=
72	  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
73	    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK κ D →
74	      sectionSub κ ((S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂) D ≤
75	        coboundarySub κ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ D
76	
77	/-- **Extension-uniform vanishing from the κ-uniform chart count.**
78	
79	The threshold transfers verbatim: `UniformChartCount`'s `b` is `UniformlyBoundedVanishing`'s
80	`b`, and at each `κ` and `D` the conclusion is `BoundedVanishing.subsingleton_h1Mod_iff`
81	applied to the chart inclusion.  No exactness hypothesis, no approximation input, no ledger.
82	
83	**What this is and is not.**  It is a genuine reduction of *cluster P's gap (2)* to a
84	statement about base-changed section spaces — the cohomological content is discharged.  It is
85	**not** a proof of extension uniformity: `UniformChartCount` is unproved at every curve, and
86	it is strictly stronger than the single-field count because `b` is quantified before `κ`.
87	Anyone reading this as "extension uniformity is closed" has misread it; a janitor made
88	exactly that conflation once already (retracted at inbox `I-0412`).
89	
90	**Relation to `ChiUnconditional` §5–§6, stated carefully.**  Those sections refute the closed
91	ledger `hledger` on a cover with a prime divisor off a chart, because `hledger` equates χ with the
92	*unbounded* `deg_k D` while the chart-finiteness binders force χ — and indeed `ℓ`
93	(`ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower`) — to be *bounded* along a tower.
94	
95	`UniformChartCount` is **not** refuted that way: it demands a subspace *inclusion*
96	`𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`, i.e. vanishing, not growth.  Vanishing content survives the tower argument; the
97	ledger's growth claim does not.  So this reduction is not vacuous for that reason.
98	
99	What remains true, and is the honest limit: `UniformChartCount` is proved at **no** curve, it is
100	strictly stronger than the single-field count (the threshold precedes `κ`), and it quantifies over
101	all divisors above `b` on every base-changed curve.  This is the sharpest honest statement of gap
102	(2) available in AJC today, and "sharpest honest" is not the same as "usable". -/

104	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
105	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
106	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
107	    (hcount : UniformChartCount C S) :
108	    UniformlyBoundedVanishing C S := by
109	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hcount
110	  refine ⟨b, fun κ _ _ D hD => ?_⟩
111	  exact (subsingleton_h1Mod_iff κ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ D).mpr

232	theorem chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
233	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
234	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
235	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
236	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
237	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
238	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))] :
239	    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) - chi k U₀ U₁ E =
240	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
241	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) := by

243	  rw [chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov E (pointDivisor P + E),
244	    sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k U₀ hP E,
245	    sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) hPinf E]

248	/-- **Off the overlap, the bump at one step is equivalent to the one-chart step being full.**
249	
250	For `P.point ∉ U₀`, the bump statement `χ(1·P+E) = χ(E) + [κ(P):k]` holds if and only if

252	exactness hypothesis.

255	`hbump` is consistent: `hbump` asserts the left side for *all* `E`, hence at every stage of the
256	tower `n·P`, and §5 shows the right side must fail for large `n` because `Γ(U₁,−) ⊆ 𝒜` is

258	inference is invalid, and `not_bump_of_notMem_left` is the correction. -/
259	theorem bump_iff_chartStep_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
260	    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
261	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
262	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
263	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
264	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
265	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))] :
266	    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P ↔
267	      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
268	        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) = residueDeg k P := by
269	  have h := chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left k U₀ U₁ hcov hP E
270	  omega

278	
279	* `Γ(U₀, −)` is frozen — the point is off `U₀` (`sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem`);

284	for **every** `n`.  But `hbump` forces `χ(n·P) = χ(0) + n·[κ(P):k]`, and `[κ(P):k] ≥ 1`
285	(`one_le_residueDeg`).  Linear growth against a fixed bound is a contradiction.
286

288	which caught this file's own docstrings claiming the opposite.  I verified the argument
289	independently before landing it. -/

294	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
295	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]

298	`sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem`. -/

    13	1. For a small site `(C, J)` and a commutative ring `R`, the degree-`n` cohomology

    18	   category, and `Sheaf.HModule.map` gives `R`-linear functoriality in `F`.

    21	3. For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, the structure sheaf of `X` as a sheaf of `k`-modules
    22	   `Scheme.moduleKSheaf` on the small Zariski site `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, by
    23	   restriction of scalars along the structure morphism, with definitional (`rfl`) access
    24	   to its sections and restriction maps.
    25	
    26	## Universe discipline
    27	
    28	Everything is single-universe: `k : Type u`, `X : Scheme.{u}`, the site `Opens X : Type u`
    29	with hom-types in `Type u`, and coefficients `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Then
    30	`Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat.{u} k)` is Grothendieck abelian relative
    31	to `u` (`ModuleCat.{u} k` is, and the site is small), hence `HasExt.{u}` holds and
    32	`Sheaf.HModule F n : Type u` with a `Module k` structure — no universe bump anywhere, so
    33	`Module.finrank k` applies directly downstream.
    34

    36	
    37	* `Sheaf.HModule` is an `abbrev` for `Abelian.Ext`, so the entire mathlib `Ext` API
    38	  (long exact sequences `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁/₂/₃`, `Ext.extClass`, the
    39	  Mayer–Vietoris machinery of `CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology`) applies
    40	  transparently; we do not rebuild any of it.

    43	  structure is carried by the explicit defs `Scheme.overAlgebraMap`/`Scheme.overModule`
